legend: Peach and Goma have taken up a new hobby recently. Sometimes they decide to get together to look at a number x$$$x$$$ and compute x⊕(x+1)$$$x \oplus (x + 1)$$$, where ⊕$$$\oplus$$$ is the bitwise XOR operator. Today they computed this value for all integers from A$$$A$$$ to B$$$B$$$ inclusive, and Peach and Goma are curious about their results. For a given number M$$$M$$$ they would like you to find the number of integers x$$$x$$$ (A≤x≤B$$$A \leq x \leq B$$$) such that x⊕(x+1)≥M$$$x \oplus (x + 1) \geq M$$$.
input: The first line contains one integer, T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤103)$$$(1 \leq T \leq 10^3)$$$, the number of test cases. Then T$$$T$$$ test cases follow.
Each test case has a single line with the integers A$$$A$$$, B$$$B$$$, M$$$M$$$ respectively, where (1≤A≤B≤109$$$1 \leq A \leq B \leq 10^9$$$, 1≤M≤109$$$1 \leq M \leq 10^9$$$).
output: T$$$T$$$ lines with one integer each denoting the number of integers x$$$x$$$ (A≤x≤B$$$A \leq x \leq B$$$) such that x⊕(x+1)≥M$$$x \oplus (x + 1) \geq M$$$ for each test case.
note: Note that 3⊕4=7$$$3 \oplus 4 = 7$$$, 4⊕5=1$$$4 \oplus 5 = 1$$$, and 5⊕6=3$$$5 \oplus 6 = 3$$$, therefore there are two integers where the computed value is greater than 2$$$2$$$.
